utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have undertaken to check, as you instructed me, and I have done so; and I owe a major apology to everyone and primarily to the Trial Chamber. I found the e-mail from the registry about the calculation of time dated 25th October, I believe that was when we had a meeting concerning translations with the Trial Chamber, and the members of my team told me that we had a discussion at that time and we wondered whether to raise that issue as well. On Friday I was prepared to swear that I had seen that e-mail, but obviously in all this chaos I must have thought it was that e-mail from the Trial Chamber. My intentions were not dishonourable, but I was prepared to swear that I had seen that e-mail last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to you for clarifying the position. Just one other matter you could confirm to us. I take it the arrangement we suggested to make available the DVDs of the interview of Mr. Lazarevic and the facility and necessary assistance to view them was provided over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tried even before Mr. Lazarevic came in to make inquiries as far as I could without breaking the rules concerning talking to the accused, but I think Mr. Lazarevic had a look at the DVDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that the recordings of the interview were made available to you and the equipment and any necessary assistance to view them also.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, last Friday I received from an officer in the Detention Unit three DVDs with instructions how to view them. I watched them and I found the segment on which I tried to concentrate last Friday, and I established it was more than we heard on Friday. I also said that I attended some of those meetings -- one of those meetings, and that was the point I was trying to make. I wanted the Trial Chamber to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we'll leave it to Mr. Hannis to ask you appropriate questions, and no doubt he'll give you the freedom to express yourself further as you wish to ensure that your position is fully explained to the Trial Chamber. I think we can now proceed with the cross-examination. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General. We will talk more about the interview, but that will be later on today. If I may, I wanted to address a matter that the Court raised I think on Friday, and this is -- General, I want to talk about the plans Grom 1 and Grom 2 and the plan that we have referred to as the plan for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. The first reference I've been able to find dealing with this sort of springs from the Supreme Defence Council meeting on the 9th of June, 1998, and this was Exhibit P1574 in evidence. And, General, I think you were aware -- at least not the specifics of that meeting, the fact that there was apparently a decision reached in that meeting in June 1998 that if the terrorism in Kosovo increased, then the army would take appropriate measures. Is that correct? Was that your knowledge and understanding back in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1998, I perceived the situation not on the basis of that meeting of the Supreme Defence Council but on the basis of what I personally and the forward command post were told by the corps commander, namely, that the army and part of the Pristina Corps would be involved in supporting MUP forces in the event terrorism escalates. But I want to say something about this Supreme Defence Council meeting too. As I said, I didn't know this session of the Supreme Defence Council had taken place, but I thought the decision was taken at the state level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain the difference to me then between the Supreme Defence Council and a decision taken at the state level.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was my understanding that there was a meeting held in Belgrade by the head of state, attended by representatives of the army, headed by the Chief of General Staff; the army commander; the corps commander; people from the police, from the Ministry of the Interior that is. That was the information available to me at that time. And when I say "state level," I mean the leadership of the state, the police and the army. And the Supreme Defence Council, as opposed to that, is a body composed of three members.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. This other group that you're talking about, we've seen an exhibit, it's Exhibit P2166 that we'll look at later on that is a meeting I think from the 29th of October, 1998, the date of the minutes I think are dated the 2nd of November. But that was a meeting that included President Milosevic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Minic, and General Pavkovic, General Samardzic, General Perisic, General Lukic, General Djordjevic. Do you recall that document? We had quite some discussion with it when I think Mr. Matkovic was here. Do you recall that one?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I believe that document was shown more than once in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that document was described as the meeting of the inter-departmental staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo, I believe. Is this group you're talking about now, is that the same group? It sounds like a similar make-up of people in terms of high-ranking police, army, and civilians.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that because what I know originating from documents. If we could compare the documents, then perhaps that could give us a confirmation, but I cannot confirm it. I knew that the corps commander and the army commander were going, and I knew the Chief of General Staff was there and people from the police; but I cannot confirm that it was the same group of people in July and in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that was a -- I want to put the background in focus. July 1998 there was a lot happening. I see from one of our exhibits in evidence 1D230, which appears to be the Official Gazette decision on establishing border areas. I think that's the 21st of July, 1998. Do you recall, was that -- was that the decision that expanded the border belt from 500 metres to a greater distance?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I did not see that Official Gazette of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Instead, through the army command, the corps received an order specifying the coordinates, trig points, and lines that were the boundaries of the new border belt, but as far as I remember that order on extending the border belt was from June, not July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is -- what was the extent of the expansion? Is that when it went from 500 metres to roughly 5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that the width of the border belt was 500 metres at any point. It used to be 100 metres, and then it was expanded to a maximum of 5 kilometres. So it was varying between 100 metres and 5 kilometres at most. I don't remember the previous width of the border belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I did misspeak, I think, when I said "500 metres." It had been 100 metres as I understand. Also, I have a note indicating that on the 21st of July there was a report in Exhibit P1510 that General Pavkovic was promoted. Do you recall him being promoted I think from major-general to lieutenant-general at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he was promoted, but the date of the promotion I really can't recall. If you have the decree or the ordinance, we can look at the document, but I do remember he was promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on the 22nd of July we have an exhibit, this is P -- I'm sorry, this is 4D100. General, we'll put this up on the screen, it's a brief document. I'll ask you to take a look at that. This is from Lieutenant-General Pavkovic to the 3rd Army command, and it's about the engagement of Pristina Corps units according to the plan for combatting terrorist forces. And it makes reference to a meeting with the president of the Federal Republic in his office on the 21st of July, where an order was given to implement the plan for combatting terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija. Did you see in that document before you came here for trial?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it -- no I didn't see it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of this -- I mean in 1998 did you hear of this plan that's called the plan for combatting terrorism or combatting terrorist forces? Did you hear of such a plan?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear what I explained at the beginning of today's session, namely, that at the highest state, military, and police level a plan was adopted to suppress terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija that would be implemented in stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it General Pavkovic who told you about that plan?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and the forward command post received information and instructions on our work from him as the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that, but did he tell you specifically about this plan for combatting terrorism and the three or five stages?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That did not happen in one go. It was as we went along and received further tasks and orders, but I knew and the corps commander informed me that the decision had been made at the level that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we've heard reference to and seen documents talking about some plans called Grom 1 and Grom 2. You have some knowledge of those, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the plan Grom 98 in stages 1 and 2, the details of which I learned here in the courtroom; but from that period I know - although I wasn't much involved in that because I wasn't in Pristina, I wasn't in the corps command - and it was the corps command that was responsible for operationalizing the plan Grom 98 in terms of formulating their own orders and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's been a little confusing for me and I think some others is the distinction, if there is one, between the plan for combatting terrorism and Grom 98 with its two phases. Those are two different things, aren't they? Isn't Grom 98 something different than the plan for combatting terrorism?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that I really wasn't very familiar with this, my understanding of this problem is as follows: When we talk about the plan for suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija by security forces, that plan and decision to engage were made at the state level. And according to that plan, some tasks were finalised by end July, and then the plan Grom 98 from General Staff to corps level covered that concept until end September. So that plan incorporated plan Grom 98 from end July, August, and later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General. Thank you. That -- that seems to make sense for me regarding some of the questions I had. I'd like to show you Exhibit 4D101, which is to the command of the 3rd Army from General Pavkovic, and this is dated the 23rd of July. And you'll see it's making reference to implementation of the second stage of the plan to eliminate terrorism in Kosovo. And it makes reference back to that 21 July meeting with President Milosevic where the order to commence implementation of the plan was given. And if you could go to item 3(A).

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think we have to go to the next page in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Under item (A) the English translation says that: "The planned engagement of the forces of the MUP and the Army of Yugoslavia was considered and accepted several times by the President and the highest leadership of the army and the MUP and during consideration of the plan (the directive and decision on the map) there were no serious objections." General, did you ever see the map that is referred to here regarding the plan for combatting terrific?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map mentioned in the text accompanies the directive, whereas the directive is of the army command and the General Staff, it's not a corps document. I'm trying to explain this to make it clear. I didn't see that directive and the decision on the map because as I said the directive is drafted by the General Staff and in some cases it may be developed by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think you made mention in your testimony on Friday and perhaps in your interview as well about having seen some map in - well, I'm not sure whether it was 1998 or 1999 - with "Joint Command" on it. Is that correct? Did you say that before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was talking about year 1998, and I said that it was a map from the corps command, though, either concerning the border belt or the interior of Kosovo and Metohija. It was a plan to lift the siege of some roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And further on in connection with this implementation of the plan to combat terrorism on the 23rd of July we have Exhibit 4D102, which if we could put up on the screen for you briefly. This is from the 3rd Army commander, General Samardzic, to the commander of the Pristina Corps, who we know was then General Pavkovic. And it's cross-referencing the document that we just looked at. And he is authorising use of the Pristina Corps units, but he has one exception which he point out because of General Pavkovic 's failure to inform President Milosevic about a certain aspect of the corps being used in unblocking roads. Were you aware of this in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I see now that this document invokes a prior document, wherein the corps commander explains to the army commander the gist of the meeting they attended together in writing, and he explains that this decision had been made at the state level. And the army commander, as I see from this document, does not approve part of that explanation and did not approve the use of corps forces - it's his right. But I see that the corps commander invoked the decision of the head of state in the prior document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I would like you to have a look at 4D137. This is dated the 28th of July, 1998. It bears the number DT-R number 23-1, and it's entitled a directive. And you'll see the reference to Grom 98 on the right-hand side. So is this, to the best of your knowledge and understanding, is this the first manifestation of Grom 98 from General Perisic and the General Staff and the army in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To that question I can only reply as much as I have learned from documents seen in the courtroom. At that time I did not see this document with this date, I saw it for the first time here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But based on your experience and knowledge in the VJ, the numbering of this order, the fact that this is number 23-1, doesn't that indicate that this document is the first in that subject number 23 for the year 1998 from the General Staff? This is the first document on this topic by virtue of the fact that it's referred to as number 1? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the reference number indicates. I cannot offer any further comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I have a question for you about the title under "directive." It says: "To deploy the Yugoslav Army for securing the State border with Albania, units and facilities in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and crush the armed rebel forces." Now, in a lot of the other orders we've seen about the fight in Kosovo in 1998, we see references to crushing the STS or the DTS, as I understand it that's the terrorist -- the Siptar terrorist forces or the Siptar -- the sabotage forces. But here General Perisic seems to be using a different term, if the translation is correct, by calling it the armed rebel forces. Am I right in that understanding?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You put it well and you read it correctly, but I don't understand if there is another question in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to make sure that the translation was correct because I think that's reflective of what we've talked about before with General Perisic and his recorded agreement that we saw in Exhibit P717 about he thought that the army shouldn't be used in these kind of actions, away from the border belt or not protecting VJ personnel and equipment, because he thought that there was a necessity of declaring a state of emergency or a state of imminent threat of war. And I think this use of the term "crush the armed rebel forces," reflects that, that he thinks this has gone beyond terrorism and has reached the stage of an armed rebellion. And that's consistent with your view at the time, right? You told us earlier that by June 1998 you thought that it -- things in Kosovo had reached such a state that it really was a factual state of emergency, even though it had not been formally declared by state authorities to be such. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What should General Lazarevic agree to because there are about five questions in there? So out of all this, does he agree with all these five or six questions you put or only with the last one concerning a document he has never seen before he said he didn't know what General Perisic's standpoint was, so what's this leading to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm looking at the transcript. I only see one question mark at the end of my paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a torturous route to get to it. I think there's substance in the point, Mr. Hannis. Could you rephrase the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, could you agree with me that the use of that term regarding the "crushing the armed rebel forces" reflects a view that the situation in Kosovo has gone beyond being a matter of simply dealing with terrorists?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is in accordance with what I know and my personal experience at the time that the forces of the armed insurgency in Kosovo and Metohija were paramilitary terrorist forces. So when the Chief of the General Staff uses this term at his strategic level, he's referring to all these terrorist forces, naming them the forces of the armed rebellion. When at a lower level orders are issued to break-up the terrorist forces in a certain location, that makes sense; but overall these terrorist forces in my military logic represent the forces of the armed insurgency.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, can we look next at Exhibit 4D456. This is also dated the 28th of July, from General Perisic, as Chief of the General Staff. It's directed to the 3rd Army command. And it's an order for him to make an assessment and work out a plan on engagement of forces pursuant to that Grom 98 document that we just looked at. And item number 3 says: "I will approve the Plan of engagement on 3 August ... At 1100 hours in the General Staff." Were you aware that this plan was being discussed or was it at a higher level than you would have had knowledge about at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this correspondence at this strategic level. I've already told you what I knew. The document speaks for itself. Of course I didn't know about this correspondence between the General Staff and the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we see this is dated -- this is numbered 23-2, so it appears to be the second in the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at 4D415.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, I'm trying to follow this -- the trail concerning this Grom 98 to see what was done about it at the 3rd Army and lower levels. We just saw in 4D456 that this was going to be approved on the 3rd of August, and 4D415 is a document from it looks like the General Staff and it has the agenda for the plan of work and approval of special documents. You'll see item 2 refers to: "Report on the decision of the commander of the 3rd Army concerning the Grom plan." Now, if we could -- I just show you that to follow-up to the next one which is 4D311, which we'll have for you in a minute here. This appears to be a telegram on the 3rd of August, 1998, from General Samardzic to the 3rd Army forward command post, Chief of Staff. And you'll see he's ordering: "A ban on the use of army units and reinforcement engaged in Kosovo in other tasks except to secure the state border, repel attacks, and protect features and all VJ forces ..." There's an exception in number two for units engaged in Junik and Jasic and a blockade on the Decani-Djakovica road. Item number 3 says: "By 1930 hours on the 3 August send back units engaged in tasks of providing support for MUP ..." Did you become aware of this? Were any of those units that were ordered to be sent back, were any of those in your area near the forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica? Did you become aware of whether or not this was happening?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with precision what combat groups in the area this refers to because items 1 and 2 where I was personally involved as the corps Chief of Staff remain in force; that refers to combatting terrorism in the border belt, deblocking communications, that is, roads, leading towards the water, and the village of Jasic. But I really cannot confirm what groups were there and were to be temporarily disengaged. It doesn't say here what groups they were, and I really don't want to speculate. I don't recall that from the time because I didn't see this document then. That's why I cannot recall these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was Junik in the border belt, within the border zone, if it's 5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 5, it's a little more, but this decision refers to Junik. It was made by the state military top leadership, and it remains in force. In item 2: "The ban does not refer to the units engaged in clearing up the border zone [as interpreted]," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think the last document that relates to this is 4D434.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I believe the -- there is a mistake in the transcript. It's 15 -- page 15, line 4, I don't think the witness said "clearing up the border zone." He said "the units engaged in that zone, in clearing that zone," referring to the Jasic and the other village, Junik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's right. I see the General agreeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, this is 4D434 and it's to the Pristina -- to the -- regarding the work of a research team. This is a research team that is supposed to go out and gather information on the actual situation in Kosovo and Metohija. Did you have any dealings with this research team in early August 1998, General? You see item 2 says they should ask for actual situation in Kosovo and Metohija and the forward command post of the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know about this research team, this scholarly research team, sent from the General Staff is that they did most of their job in Pristina; but I recall that they spent a day in Djakovica and visited some of the units defending the state border in order to gather scholarly experience about to what extent the units can stand psychological and physical strain. So this was a specialised team from the military medical academy for preventive psycho-social or whatever its name was, that was another research team; but this research team, as I recall, visited for a day in order to collect these experiences. What I want to say is when a research team is mentioned, that's scientific research, scholarly research, they were engaged in because I recognise some of these people, they're from the institute of strategic research and they're linked to the General Staff. It's at the highest level of military education.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if you would look two lines above the word "order," the English translation says: "The team will research terrorist operations in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija." Now, maybe I've made a faulty assumption, but in light of what we were just looking at before we've had -- we've had the directive from General Perisic about making plans that deal with crushing the armed rebel forces. We saw General Samardzic's telegram ordering that certain units that were supporting MUP forces be sent back, and we know from other evidence in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to avoid barking up the wrong tree, could we please read again this sentence that has to do with research because I think a correct translation will give us at least two meanings. It's ambiguous and then perhaps the General will clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General, could you read out that sentence for us, then, two sentences above the word "order."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The team will work on research in connection with terrorist activities on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I guess, General, the reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as long as we've got a little break here I want to make an objection of my own. You stopped me the other day during one of my examinations by suggesting that what I was doing was making a submission rather than asking questions of the witness. Mr. Hannis has yet to show this witness a document that he's ever seen before today or that he knows anything about, but he's making a very well-constructed argument regarding the OTP's position in the case with the Perisic orders and things of that nature. So it looks to me like what's going on here this morning is an OTP submission and not anything to do with this witness. He's yet to be able to answer a question about any of these documents because he never saw them before and knew nothing of what was going on behind them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: To the extent there may be some force in what you have said, it does not apply to the current one because the witness is being asked about something that he specifically knows of. Whether or he has seen the document before. He says that this group spent a day in Djakovica and visited some of the units defending the state border, so he's speaking from personal experience. But we do note the point you make as I hope Mr. Hannis will note it because I think there's some substance in what's being said. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hear that, but I hope that as I go along you will see that what I'm trying to ask here relates to what is going to come in some further documents as well as relating back to the ones that we've been following along with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, General, having read that sentence the translation we got is pretty similar to what I have in writing here. I suggest to you the reason this research team was sent out was to find out how serious the terrorist problem was because there was some disagreement at other levels about whether or not the army should be engaged in supporting MUP in dealing with this problem. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is quite contrary to what the Prosecutor has just said. Bearing in mind these people's scholarly profession, I understood that they were studying terrorism on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and the experiences of the units of the 3rd Army and Pristina Corps in this respect. I have absolutely no knowledge that they were investigating or researching whether the army was being used in compliance with the decision of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to draw attention to a misinterpretation, because when you look at the composition of the team, or rather, mistranslation, some, or rather, the titles of these persons are missing, and this might also mislead us, Your Honour. In the Serbian version - and you can ask that the General read this out - you will see that these people have titles, scholarly titles, academic titles, which are missing in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, if you look at the introductory paragraph at the top of the screen, in the third line the composition of the team is laid out. Could you read the identity of the various members of the team, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The composition of the team, Lieutenant-Colonel Bozidar Forcan master of science, head of team; Lieutenant-Colonel Branislav Djordjevic, master of science, deputy head of team; Lieutenant-Colonel Petar Kostic, who was a bachelor of science; and Majors -- Dr. Mitar Kovac and Major -- Dr. Zlatan Jeremic team members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I want to show you Exhibit P1419, General, and I think I got this one out of sequence because this is actually dated the 1st of August, 1998. And you'll see this is from General Pavkovic to the 3rd Army forward command post requesting approval to launch the third stage of the plan to curb terrorism in Kosovo, and he mentions in the first paragraph that it was decided at a meeting of the Joint Command on the 31st of July to launch the third stage of the plan on 2 August. And looking at what was decided, it talks about operations in certain areas and item number 2 is exerting psychological pressure on the terrorist forces in Junik village by continuing the blockade. General, can you tell, does this request relate to the telegram we saw from General Samardzic on -- dated the 3rd of August or is this unrelated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Their Honours leave, I would have to look at this and make a comparison. I really can't answer with precision whether this refers to the document where he prohibits further engagement, if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, if we could look at 4D415 in the B/C/S side by side. I see Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honours, in all fairness to the witness he said he would need to compare. So he should be provided with both documents, and then he can probably give the answer. Because shifting it on the screen, it doesn't help -- it doesn't help me much at least. I'm not able to remember the previous document when I'm looking at the document now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I don't have a hard copy of 415. I do have a hard copy of 1419 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's all we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- I can give to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't solve Mr. Zecevic's particular personal problem, but it solves the problem for the witness, who really matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now -- and I think I have referred to the wrong item, because I wanted -- perhaps it was 4D311?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it is 311.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, you think it's 311 on the screen, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, I think the one you want is 4D311.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that's right. My apologies to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There, General, you see the telegram on the screen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your problem is also solved now, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor asked me whether this document on the right-hand side of the monitor is connected to the one on the left-hand side. Some locations correspond, namely, Junik and Jasic, but I see that the army commander does not mention the Drenica, Jablanica, and Likovac actions. So I cannot be completely sure whether this is it or whether there was an intervening document between these two. Because the corps commander is informing the army commander that this is the third stage, the third phase, which had been adopted previously, and asks in the last sentence the army commander to approve the realization or implementation of the plan. I really cannot be a hundred per cent certain whether the army commander's reply has to do with this request coming from the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General, thank you. And you can't tell from Samardzic's telegram whether the reference to supporting MUP, what actions the MUP are involved in, that item number, I think it's 3, refers to, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In item 3 the army commander says that the units engaged in tasks of support to the MUP should return to their areas of deployment, but I don't see where that is; and the corps commander is only now proposing Drenica and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. Next I want to go to Exhibit P1435, which is in evidence. This is a document from General Pavkovic dated the 22nd of September, 1998, to the 3rd Army command, personally to the commander. And it's about the implementation of stage 5 of the plan to combat terrorism. Now, you'll see in item number 1 there's a reference to a meeting presided over by President Milosevic regarding the plan for implementing stage 5 and a reference that that plan contemplated three additional BGs, combat groups, to be moved down to Kosovo; a relocation of Battle Group 211. And lastly under item 1 the indication that after that meeting with President Milosevic, General Perisic, the Chief of the General Staff, issued a verbal order regarding how those battle groups were going to be formed because it was impossible to move other battle groups into Kosovo and Metohija. Now, General, were you aware of any of this, that General Pavkovic was seeking to have additional battle groups formed and brought into Kosovo from outside of Kosovo? Did he discuss that with you in September 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said on Friday there was the fifth stage as well, and this document refreshes my memory. I remember the fifth stage involved additional in-depth security of the state border with Albania, and I remember that the corps command evaluating possible further developments suggested to the 3rd Army and up to strengthen these locations mentioned here, Planeja and the other ones. A combat group arrived very shortly before the arrival of the OSCE mission to that location, Planeja, but it was not the 3rd Battalion of military police, it was another group from the army. That is the first bullet point that I'm talking about. So I remember these requests and I remember that there was a reinforcement of the in-depth security of the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember -- from the way I read this, it sounds as though this plan for additional combat groups to be brought in from the outside appears to have been discussed with President Milosevic at the meeting, and it's after the meeting that General Perisic seems to be changing that - isn't that right - by means of an oral order or a verbal order? Because he says it was impossible to move other battle groups into Kosovo and Metohija. Did General Pavkovic complain about that to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this and I remember this in a very specific way, namely, that the corps command suggested a reinforcement with two combat groups from outside the corps, whereas the 3rd Army command - and I see here in the document the Chief of General Staff - proposed instead that we form our own combat groups from our troops. And I want to point out to the honourable Trial Chamber that in order to form combat groups we need a decision, not from the corps commander but from the army commander or the Chief of General Staff. And I see that they propose that we form our own combat groups and provide our own additional security on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as you follow along in the document you'll see that the next day apparently General Pavkovic repeated his request at the 3rd Army command meeting, and talked about having another two battle groups. But he says no response was given or any solution suggested. Paragraph 3 then mentions that the 3rd Army command meeting on the 7th of September he proposed if he couldn't have two battle groups moved down to Kosovo, that they engage two provisional release formations from the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the General cannot follow the last passage read by Mr. Hannis. We need to scroll down or maybe turn the page so that the General can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can hand him a hard copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I apologise, General. I didn't mean to get ahead of you. Are you with me now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see point 3. It is also consistent with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have a situation in which both the Prosecutor and the witness see something that neither the Trial Chamber nor counsel do. We should all see it. It should be on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree, we all should see it. Can we go to the second page of both the B/C/S and the English. Well, I'm sorry, item number 3 in the English is on the first page that we were on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's on page 1 of the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General, were you about to say something about item 3?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah. Were you aware of this second meeting between General Pavkovic and the 3rd Army command on the 7th of September, again trying to get some additional battle groups formed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the meeting, but point 3 confirms what I said a moment ago, namely, that the commander had asked for two new combat groups because the Chief of General Staff made a verbal order and said we should set up these combat groups ourselves. And the corps commander is informing the army commander thereof. So the decision to form these combat groups has to be made at a higher level. As for the meeting of 7th September, I wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Then item number 4 at the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S and on the top of page 2 in the English, it makes reference to a briefing on implementing stage 5 of the plan, which was given at a meeting of the ZK for Kosovo and Metohija, which I suggest to you is the Joint Command, on 10th September 1998. And it says: " ... Other command organs pointed out that the VJ had not carried out two of its duties under the Plan ..." Now, before we go to page 2 for the other Serbian speakers, can you tell us, do you know what the reference to "other command organs" was in item 4 here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can try to interpret linguistically and logically, but not factually. Here in point 4 the person who wrote this document says that there was a meeting of the ZK, I suppose it was a meeting of the police and the army that we call the Joint Command, on the 10th of September and other organs, participants in that meeting, organs of the command it says -- it doesn't make sense when you put it this way, not to me. But other participants in that meeting seems to have noticed that from this plan that was approved at a higher level, the army failed to live up to two of its obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2 of B/C/S in e-court.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army did not set up a helicopter unit for quick interventions, as had been ordered on the 31st of August by the head of state; and second, two combat groups were not brought into Kosovo and Metohija, and this seems to indicate that that too had been ordered at the higher level, the highest state level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, General, we've talked on Friday I think a little bit about the rapid intervention units and the helicopters. Do you remember that discussion? And we saw a document from General Pavkovic to General Samardzic regarding that. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that document, and I remember our brief discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, I'd like to go just briefly to Exhibit P1468, which are those Joint Command meetings in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tell you at page 108 of the English is the beginning page for this meeting on the -- a meeting on the 13th of September, 1998, and General Pavkovic is speaking. And we'll see the part I want on the following page, 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I'll try and give you a hard copy of the B/C/S page, which is page 8505 are the last four digits. I could hand this to you. And, General, can you see at the top that is a meeting of 13th September, 1998, and General Pavkovic appears to be the first speaker. And I would like you to read the last two bullet points under him. The first one starts out in English with: "In connection with the repeated request ..." Could you read that for us, see how our translation is.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With regard to the repeated," and then a couple of letters are missing, there's a dot there, but it can be understood as you read it, "repeated." So "with regard to the repeated request for ..." This is some sort of acronym or abbreviation, "the command of the 3rd Army and the General Staff did not accept or did not approve."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The translation in English regarding the HE is suggested that possibly HE in this context refers to helicopters. Would you agree that that's possible?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If HE, if this is indeed HE, although it looks like an S to me, but if it's HE it could be short for helicopter, but I cannot really make out that that is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could you read the next bullet point for us, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Two combat groups that we requested have not been approved to us." I think it says "approved."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And right below that you see Mr. Sainovic is listed as speaking. Could you read that for us, because part of the English translation is indicated as being illegible. I don't know if you can read it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In" this word was abbreviated. I cannot read it " - the task regarding HE," it's probably helicopters, "we are not in a position to implement, to carry out, because we did not get them." I'm trying my best to make it out because some letters are missing, but that could be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Fila, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waited for the end of the answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. What is the question, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can't spend this time, valuable court time going over translations like this, Mr. Hannis, unless there's a question at the end of it. Mr. Ackerman has already made the point that this is the stage at which you should be asking focused questions in cross-examination of matters that the witness can give us personal insight into.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I'm trying to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The -- so we see General Pavkovic in this Joint Command meeting continuing the discussion about the problem that he writes about in P1435 to General Samardzic. Will you -- can we return to 1435, General, P1435. And on the second page near the bottom it has the phrase "we propose." Right above that the English translation says: "Moreover, we are giving the members of the ZK for Kosovo and Metohija the opportunity to report to the president of the FRY that the VJ has not carried out its duties under the plan." Did General Pavkovic complain to you about this problem with the battle groups and -- or the combat groups in the rapid intervention units? Did he complain to you about the difficulties that was causing him?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The corps commander did not complain to me in those terms. He told me, and we all knew. You see the last point, he suggests that we form our own combat groups for Planeja and Goruzup from the troops of the 549th Motorised Brigade. It was decided that we do this on our own. He didn't complain that we were not allowed to form this unit using personnel from the army and the police, as they term it here the rapid intervention team. This team consists of both forces, the army provides helicopters and there were teams on duty from both the police and the army. That was the plan, I knew about the plan, but he didn't complain at this meeting with the commander of the 3rd Army, he didn't complain to Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he didn't mention that to you before you went to the Joint Command meetings on the 17th, 18th, 19th of September?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember. I came to Pristina after such a long time to inform him about a large number of issues, and even with the best of efforts I cannot recall everything that we discussed. I know about the general issues, state border, this problem of how to find additional forces, that was the main point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, weren't you interested in your job in connection with the state border and the possibility of having rapid intervention units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood that idea, those were not supposed to be units. It's a unit, a company-strong unit, and it was not meant for the border; it was meant for the territory of Kosovo and Metohija wherever parts of the army or the police were in jeopardy or perhaps installations and facilities. And it was our position that the border should always be manned with sufficient forces to stop further escalation of terrorism and incursions from Albania. That's what I know from that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You recall when we talked Friday about that, that we saw the document from General Pavkovic reflecting the fact that after the Joint Command meetings on the 19th and 20th of September he had raised again the issue about rapid intervention capabilities. You don't recall that being a matter that he brought to your attention because you were attending meetings at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to be as specific as I could. I really don't remember that that was the main topic that I came to discuss. I was to propose and prepare a complex study for securing the state border, and that was to be implemented over the following few months.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question wasn't really whether or not that was the main topic you were going to talk about. My question was: Was this a topic that General Pavkovic discussed with you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some point I was informed that this helicopter unit was to be set up. It was only one helicopter that could carry a maximum of 25 people, 50 people in two trips, but I did not participate in the further operationalization of that idea, so I cannot confirm whether we discussed it on the 19th. I would say that I was informed of that idea earlier than the 19th, but to the best of my recollection it was not clear at that time. I know about the problem, but I don't know when I first heard it from the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In connection with the five phases of the plan for combatting terrorism, at the beginning of the various phases are you aware that there were meetings to discuss the assignments and the task for the VJ and MUP units that were going to be involved in those activities? Did you know that they were meetings with both the MUP and VJ commanders present to discuss those pertinent tasks?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was coordination and exchange of information between the command of the Pristina Corps and individual brigade commanders on one hand and certain agencies from the police, the MUP staff and MUP detachments, that there were frequent meetings starting back in July, starting with the level of army down to corps level, et cetera, and what you just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And before each phase those meetings took place in Pristina with documents being handed out to both the army and the MUP commanders, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that the execution of each stage was analysed at the level of the 3rd Army or at the level of the corps command or MUP, and I cannot confirm that anyone collated these new documents to another force concerning the following stages. And as far as I remember, I did not attend those analytical meetings at the end of every stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall break and resume at ten to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next document I'm going to use is Exhibit P939, which are VJ collegium meeting minutes from the 21st of January. And I'll start first with page 9 of the English and page 8 of the B/C/S. General, before I ask you a question about that, just with regard to the combat groups that we were talking about before. Can you tell us, BG 211, from what -- from what unit was that composed? What was the 211th?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat group 211 was a temporary unit from the 211th Armoured Brigade -- it was equivalent to two or three mixed companies, some mechanised, some tank, some support. I can't recall precisely the composition, but it was a temporary composition of the 211th Armoured Brigade of the Nis Corps of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that -- where was the -- where was the home garrison for the 211th, it was in Nis?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured brigade, 211th, was deployed in the Stevan Sindjelic barracks in Nis, where I started my career as a lieutenant-colonel in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a junior -- as a lieutenant, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, General, when did you take up your duties with the Pristina Corps as commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed the duty of commander of the Pristina Corps on the 9th of January, 1999, and I signed the record on the handover of duties on the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to show you this Exhibit P939 which is a VJ collegium meeting of the 21st of January, and there's a discussion in that meeting as you might imagine about events at Racak. Beginning on page 8 of the B/C/S you'll see that General Obradovic is speaking. And he makes reference to the 8th Federal Mechanised Tank Squad. Can you tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably a mistranslation. Just give me ten seconds to read the sentence, and then I'll respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian language the record is quite difficult to understand. It's a stenographic record, but what I can say based on this is that General Obradovic is reporting that an exercise was carried out at the department level on topic 8. On topic 8, the mechanised section, that's an exercise not to support the MUP; it's a planned exercise in the general area where the combat group of the 244th [as interpreted] Mechanised Brigade was employed -- was deployed. It's the lowest-level exercise from squad level upwards. So this is actually a squad exercise on topic 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to whom was this squad subordinate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This squad was part of the combat group of the 244th Mechanised Brigade, which according to the agreement of October was located at the Dulje pass to secure the Crnoljevska gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it possible for you to read, please, the section, read out aloud the section from the start of what Obradovic says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "General, sir, this was an exercise which was not meant to support the MUP forces. It was a tactical exercise of a squad and it says precisely, literally, on the Dulje and village ... axis kilometre 988," it should be trigonometer, an exercise was carried out on topic 8 a conscientious tank of the mechanised squad and the exercise was carried out according to plan and the unit returned to its area of deployment. Therefore, it is not any sort of activity to support the MUP forces. Where it says conscientious, what they really mean is in coordinated action with, but I'm now telling you my opinion, what I think it should say, not what it actually says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Before it goes off the screen, line 34, and 34, line 5, both times the general mentioned the 203rd Mechanised Brigade, whereas the transcript reads 244th, it was the 203rd -- 243 -- 243rd --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be 243.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The 243rd Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to get to that. General, you'll see the next entry is from General Dimitrijevic who says: "A part of the 243rd Combat Group was also carrying out an exercise in accordance with the plan on 15 January. It also said' planned exercise,'" correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here -- I have to make use of what is on the screen. "According to plan, a part of the 243rd Combat Group carried out an exercise on the 15th of January, and it also said 'planned exercise.'".

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, were you involved in any of the discussions post-Racak about whether or not any elements or forces of the VJ had been involved in any way in the events on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in the conversation as far as I can recall, but the corps command delivered a regular daily operative report to the command of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall what was reported in that daily report from your corps command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, the corps command reported that combat group -- the combat group of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade on the 14th and 15th and perhaps the following day carried out its exercises in the area in two directions, on two axes; that the units carrying out the exercises were very small and that they were attacked by terrorist forces; that the OSCE mission had been informed; and that the unit did not participate in the action to support the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't want to interrupt, but I'm afraid that if we continue we will run into problems because we did not deal with Racak. Racak has been left out of the indictment, and the Defence did not focus on documents or anything else in connection with Racak. And now my learned friend is asking specifically about Racak and evidence concerning Racak, so I'm afraid we may be now getting into an area for which we are not prepared. I don't think that my learned friend should be allowed to continue in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Bakrac, that there have been a number of questions about command and control responsibility in relation to events at Racak and that what has not been explored at all has been the exact nature of the event itself. At that moment it seems to me that Mr. Hannis's questions do not go beyond the area that's already been open to exploration by both sides, and therefore we shall allow him to continue with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Actually, I think I got an answer for the part I wanted, Your Honour. I'll go to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, at page 10 of the English and it's also page 10 of the B/C/S, this is General Ojdanic speaking - I hope it's General Ojdanic speaking, yes - and I'm reading from the fourth line of the English: "A number of steps need to be undertaken in order to prove that the army did not take part. I was intrigued by this action, or operation, or whatever you want to call it, in Racak village, and I personally asked the corps commander to send me a report on where the army was and what the army was doing at that moment." Do you recall -- that's a reference to you, isn't it, do you recall General Ojdanic asking you to send him a special report about Racak?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one reads this like that, I can't recall. I can't confirm that the Chief of the General Staff called me up as the corps commander, which doesn't mean that an order was not sent from the General Staff through the 3rd Army or directly that a special report be submitted. But I cannot confirm that I directly received this task from the Chief of the General Staff as the corps commander to explain the situation. I remember only the regular operative report, and I remember that the command of the 3rd Army a little later on, around the 20th of January or thereabouts, delivered a special report to the General Staff at the request either of the chief or deputy of the Chief of Staff. I'm not sure. I've seen that document here in the courtroom, but I don't know what exhibit number it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, you would agree with me, would you not, that Racak at that time was a very significant event, subject to a lot of international media and controversy. It was the hottest topic in Kosovo and Serbia at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor is asking a very broad question. I will say that at some point later on it really did become a major topic, but when it comes to the Pristina Corps I want to say that in the first few days no one from the OSCE mission asked anyone about that action. For the corps command, it was an action which was an attempt to arrest terrorists who before that had killed several policemen. This action was carried out, and all the other information came from the media. When it comes to what I knew and what the corps command knew, what I want to say is that the corps command did not deal with that issue, the issue of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, but, General, this is basically your first week on the job as the commander of the Pristina Corps. This is a very significant event with a lot of international and media attention. And are you telling me that you do not remember that the Chief of the General Staff, your highest boss, personally asked you for a report about it? You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll repeat what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, can you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Certainly I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Going on General Ojdanic says: "It had to be studied in detail and I studied this report and I wept back to the special report," and I'm skipping. It says that: "The army did not take part but there was a combat group at the entrance to Crnoljevo as you're coming from Stimlje. And when the MUP started the operation towards Racak village, it was fully justified for them to take this wider sector for a flexible defence and, reportedly, there were no other activities." Do you know which combat group that was at the entrance to Crnoljevo?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, absolutely, that one combat group was in the Stimlje area. Part of the only combat group covering the entry to the Crnoljevo gorge and the Dulje pass, that was only one combat group consisting of two parts. So that was a smaller part of the combat group of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade, it was the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying that General Ojdanic is mistaken here when he makes reference to a combat group, rather, it was some smaller component thereof. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying he said that. That's what it says here, but as we have seen, whoever was taking those notes didn't take things -- many things down properly. What I'm saying is it was not a combat group, but rather a smaller part of that one combat group under the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, these are the collegium minutes. Are you saying that they were not properly recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I want to point out to Your Honours is that you asked me a little while ago to read out a sentence which was illogical, nonsensical. And I can't say whether the Chief of the General Staff actually said that or whether the person taking the minutes just wrote it down like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, my understanding regarding these collegium minutes is that they are tape recorded and then a transcript is prepared from the tape. Is that your understanding as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how this was done in technical terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's move on to page 11 at the English and it's page 10 in the B/C/S. I believe it's paragraph 2. General Ojdanic is speaking and he says: "If the forces have to be used, nobody is denying that right to those who have the right to order it, but that means that if this joint staff command or whatever decided that the operation in Racak village could not be carried out without the assistance of the Yugoslav Army, we know very well who must be asked for approval, if the FRY president orders, in spite of all the risk, that the army be used, this decision must be carried out, bearing in mind the restrictions contained in the agreement, neither Pavkovic nor I have the right. Anyone can do it but then he must take on all responsibility for the resulting consequences ..." Here General Ojdanic seems to be making reference to the Joint Command in January 1999. And I take it from your earlier answers, you weren't aware of the Joint Command functioning in 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Their Honours' leave, may I read in Serbian in paragraph 2 half a sentence which says: "But this means if this joint staff," it doesn't say here "Joint Command." I really cannot identify what this joint staff refers to. So in answer to your question, there was no Joint Command in 1990 [sic] nor do I know about the existence of a Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you -- yeah. Could you read that sentence beginning: "If the forces have to be used ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "If the forces have to be used, nobody's denying that right to those who have the right to order it, but that means that if this joint staff command, or whatever, decided that the operation in Racak village could not be carried out without the assistance" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's enough for present purposes. It has been accurately translated. I wondered if there was another problem. You've now answered the question that you were asked to say that you did not know about the existence of a Joint Command I think in 1999, isn't that correct, rather than 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in 1999, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a comment on the translation of the word "akcija" it's been interpreted for some time as "operation," but this can have an influence in view of the level of planning. In the Serbian language the word "akcija" means something quite different from what is called action here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have been over this problem earlier and are alert to it. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe there's a could be a critical issue as to the translation. The translation comes out "joint" for both "zdruzeni" and "zajednicka," which is not the same word in the Serbian and then in the Serbian original there is actually a comma after "zdruzeni" or "combined staff," and then it says ", komanda." So I think if we look at the original document we see that what's appearing in the transcript is not actually correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well there is a comma in the English as well. Your argument is over the translation of the word joint or combined and that is a matter we have already said will have to be addressed in submissions in due course. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's another significant error, line 41 -- page 41, page 7. In the Serbian version after "joint staff," as my colleague Mr. Ivetic has explained, there should be a comma, and then it should say "command."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the actual document there is a comma. Just because the transcriber here, working under enormous pressure, doesn't put a comma in there, Mr. Bakrac, we don't need to stop the proceedings and have it rectified. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on. Mr. Fila now.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just assist the Court. I'm not going to interfere much. This is now the third term. We have "zajednicka," joint; we have "objednijena," combined; and we have "zdruzeni," joint or combined. Now, these are three terms now, all of them translated as "joint." What General Lazarevic used was "objedinjena," combined. I'm emphasising this because you heard it. If that is the same thing, then Mr. Hannis is right. Now we have three problems with translation, not two. You know the Cyrillic script, you can read it. I'm sorry for bothering you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are alert to this problem and have already said on more than one occasion that submissions will have to be made about it and we'll deal with these as they arise. In addition, if the matter can be further clarified in re-examination, then that opportunity is also available to Mr. Bakrac. So let's proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, continuing on that same page, 10, in the B/C/S and it's page 12 of the English in the middle, still General Ojdanic speaking, and he says --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think there's a translation issue here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- but the word for "joint" appears to be "zajednicka" in this one. "There is yet another option. There is an option, the Joint Command down there whereby the president orders me and I have to know it immediately and it says by order of the President of the FRY, due to the seriousness of the situation, such and such forces and assets of some of the Pristina Corps units shall be engaged and everything is fine and there is no problem." Now, here it's clear he's using the term "Joint Command," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, can you help us with a possible typographical error here, because I have a note when we discussed this previously with another witness where it says "the Joint Command down there whereby the president orders me," I'm told that that perhaps could be a transposition of the two letters for that word in Serbian and it may actually mean "orders them." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only read what is written here with the leave of the Trial Chamber, otherwise I didn't really understand what you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, then, did I read it correctly when I said: "The Joint Command down there whereby the president orders me"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That part is correct, looking at the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go two paragraphs farther down. It says: "As far as this other issue is concerned," and I think you'll see what it refers to, "did they choose the most appropriate time or not. I asked Pavkovic the same thing and I asked Lazo what was the meaning of a mechanised platoon on the march as a subject, is this platoon learning anything or is it just being exposed to danger, is this a demonstration of force and what's the purpose of such an exercise?" A couple questions, is Lazo -- is that your nickname? Is he referring to you there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think this is referring to what Obradovic was talking before about that mechanised tank squad engaged in an exercise. So he says he asked you about what this was for. Do you recall talking to General Ojdanic about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood, this is the collegium meeting of the 21st of January, at least that's what I heard in my headphones, although the text says "24th December" at the bottom. I remember that at some point on one occasion the general -- the Chief of General Staff asked me how to protect units, generally speaking, both in movement and when they are performing combat activities. I remember that. But I don't remember what you just asked me, whether I talked on the 15th or at the time of Racak with the Chief of General Staff about the operation in Racak. It's not that he's suggesting that to me, but as an officer, as a general who knows how security should be provided, we discussed a broader topic, flank security and how that is arranged. Yes, we discussed that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you don't recall him discussing with you before the 21st of January, 1999, the specific issue of this mechanised platoon being on an exercise? You don't recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall about that period, the 15th or just after the 15th. I remember discussing the general problem of performing exercises, and in particular providing security in movement through gorges, such as the Crnoljevo gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General. I want to move on to page 21 in the B/C/S, it's page 24 of the English. This relates to some answers you gave last week when you were talking about what the army and the Pristina Corps were doing in early 1999. You told us that you had good intelligence and information that the KLA was planning a spring operation. And I don't have the precise wording here, but in one of your answers you said that the army wasn't doing anything. You were living as though you would not have a war for a hundred years. Do you recall saying words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that I said something like that in the context of the fact that 50 to 60 per cent of the corps were in the areas of the peacetime location and they were engaged in their regular combat build-up. That was my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see that General Bojovic is talking about the fact that KLA is getting ready for its spring, that NATO is threatening and getting ready for its spring, and he says: "We must literally prepare for this spring." He talks about options.
